title: Kakao
summary: Korean messaging and internet group building Korean-language models for its own services.
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

Kakao owns the dominant messaging app in Korea, which gives it a distribution channel for assistants, search and commerce features built on its own language models. The AI effort is defensive as much as offensive: if conversational interfaces absorb search and messaging, the platform must own the model layer to keep the user relationship. Competition from Naver and global assistants is direct.

Technology Exposure

  • Korean-language foundation models
  • KakaoTalk assistant and search features
  • Content and commerce services

What To Watch

  • Monetisation of AI features without user churn
  • Competition with Naver's HyperCLOVA
  • Content and platform regulation

Record Notes

Editorial brief compiled 19 November 2026 from company disclosures, agency publications and press reporting. Figures are as reported by those sources and have not been independently audited; no live market data is used.

businessMeaning: A messaging platform that owns its model can defend the interface; one that rents a model hands the relationship to a third party.
investmentLens: Listed; the AI line is a cost centre until it lifts advertising or commerce revenue per user.
